recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Further edits would be redundant unless a future work group decision changes the Element/BackboneElement boundary or requests additional generated StructureDefinition wording beyond the current narrative and spreadsheet definitions.
issue_request: FHIR-7401 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core DSTU1 clarification asking the specification to distinguish Element from BackboneElement because their definitions sounded nearly identical; the accepted resolution was to improve the definitions.
initial_application: The Jira comment records SVN revision 6442. In git-svn history, commit 08a6113725dd1d7815bf53d094cc70114d8ed281 applied that revision by updating source/backboneelement.html to say BackboneElement is defined as part of a resource definition, that datatype elements do not use it, and that Patient.contact is an example.
additional_context: The old standalone Element and BackboneElement pages were later folded into source/types.html by cbdf7d1e55dc4bfa1dc30fc526edee0491e05782. Later same-family issue FHIR-17017 tightened the BackboneElement wording further and is already represented on the combined branch by commit 20ab87310ee300f0e493ea873ce2cdcf38d0f9cd. The active fhir.ini configuration keeps Element and BackboneElement in build scope as normative abstract infrastructure types and maps BackboneElement to the types page.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/types.html explains that Element covers datatype and resource-structure descendants in resources, while BackboneElement is for complex elements declared as part of resource definitions and excludes datatype elements; source/datatypes/element.xml and source/datatypes/backboneelement.xml are consistent with that distinction.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive issue tightened the same BackboneElement definition to exclude datatype elements more explicitly; it is already audited on the combined branch.
